page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled at 2 threads per core. The CPU operates at a base speed of 2.3 GHz and is supported by a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. The instance is configured with 30.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.75 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across most standard compute and memory operations. The instance achieved a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 2173.49 and a multi-core score of 8882.75. Memory bandwidth tests show 690.5 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 61.57 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 36.0 GB/sec for large-block writes. Notably, single-threaded gzip compression at 35.04 GB/sec and single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 15.25 GB/sec rank in the top 25% and top 10% respectively. In LLM inference tests using a small 135M model, text generation reached a top-tier speed of 352.64 tokens/sec, though text generation with a medium 7B model dropped to a weak 7.21 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4n-standard-8 offers a balanced resource density suitable for general-purpose workloads without the premium cost of dedicated GPU or high-capacity local NVMe storage. The inclusion of advanced CPU instruction sets, such as Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), provides hardware-accelerated execution for cryptography and vector math without requiring discrete accelerators. This makes the instance well-suited for workloads such as static web serving, database operations, moderate-scale LLM prompt processing, and general-purpose computational tasks.

This instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for balanced workloads, making it suitable for static web serving, database operations, and general-purpose applications requiring advanced vector and matrix extensions.
